The surface is assembled from a sphere with 2g holes and g annuli.
Each red α curve is the closed core of an annulus. The β curves run across
the sphere chart and the annuli. A black point is one signed mathematical
intersection; open points marked xᵢ are attachment ports, not extra crossings.
There are no projection crossings. The outside of the sphere chart includes ∞.

The outer boundary of annulus i attaches to Bᵢ+, and its inner boundary to
Bᵢ−. With t the α cyclic parameter, θ on the annulus is −2πt; θ on
the sphere is +2πt at Bᵢ+ and −2πt at Bᵢ−. The base has orientation
−dx∧dy and each annulus dx∧dy. Thus α runs clockwise and a positive
β crossing runs from the inner to the outer boundary.

```{julia}
using Topology
const H = Topology.Heegaard
const ROOT = dirname(Base.active_project())
const SOURCE = joinpath(ROOT, "artifacts", "heegaard", "app")

function atlas_example(id)
    diagram = H.certify_heegaard(H.load_heegaard(joinpath(SOURCE, "$id.hgd.json")))
    fixed_plot = H.load_layout(joinpath(SOURCE, "$id.hgd.layout.json"), diagram)
    chart = H.surface_chart(diagram, fixed_plot)
    (diagram=diagram, fixed_plot=fixed_plot, chart=chart)
end
```

## S³

```{julia}
s3 = atlas_example("S3")
H.plot(s3.chart)
```

## L(5,2)

```{julia}
lens = atlas_example("L5_2")
lens.chart
```

## Poincaré

The inherited Poincaré fixture has source-transcribed cyclic words and a
candidate region decoration. Its saved feasible geometry is fixture-scoped.
Rendering preserves that provenance and does not certify the source attribution
or establish a complete general router.

```{julia}
poincare = atlas_example("Poincare")
poincare.chart
```

## Compare the original alpha-cut view

```{julia}
poincare.fixed_plot
```

The plots above reuse the versioned fixed-100 elastic geometry, producing the
same SVG as the dedicated web page. To compute a new fixed-production plot
from a feasible seed, the matching entrance is:

```julia
figure = H.plot(diagram, feasible; view=:surface)
# The existing default H.plot(diagram, feasible) still gives the alpha-cut view.
```

## Save the exact displayed SVG

```{julia}
output = joinpath(ROOT, "artifacts", "heegaard", "full_curves", "qmd")
mkpath(output)
for (id, sample) in [("S3", s3), ("L5_2", lens), ("Poincare", poincare)]
    H.render(sample.chart; backend=:svg, path=joinpath(output, "$id.svg"))
end
(genus=poincare.chart.genus,
 intersections=length(poincare.chart.intersections),
 hash=poincare.chart.diagram_hash)
```

Scope: currently certified closed Heegaard diagrams with g curves in each
family, a validated alpha-cut layout, and at least one intersection on every
β curve. Raw/decorated codes are not promoted implicitly. Zero-intersection
β components need additional geometric data and are rejected. Certification
here means the existing software checks, not a new proof of completeness of
meridian systems. Layout coordinates remain derived data.
